findings.evidence: Lines 443-457: `hγ` occurs only in `have hγR := hγ.mono ...` and `have hγL := hγ.mono ...`; everything after uses `hγR`/`hγL`. Compare the sibling intro `hasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt_of_lipschitzOnWith` (line 428), which already takes arbitrary one-sided pieces `Icc c t` / `Icc t d`, and the file's own header (lines 18-24) stating the point is crossings 'at a corner, where the two one-sided tangents may differ'. Grep shows no consumer of `hasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt_of_contDiffOn` in the repo, so restating it costs nothing.
findings.fix: State it on the two one-sided pieces: `{c t d : ℝ} (hct : c < t) (htd : t < d) (hγR : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc t d)) (hγL : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc c t)) : HasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt γ t`. The existing proof body goes through verbatim with `hγR`/`hγL` in place of `hγ.mono ...`, since `uniqueDiffOn_Icc`, `convex_Icc` and `isCompact_Icc` only need `c < t` and `t < d`.
findings.issue: `hasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt_of_contDiffOn` requires `ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc (t - ε) (t + ε))`, a symmetric two-sided C² neighborhood, but the proof uses it only via `hγ.mono` to `Icc t (t + ε)` and `Icc (t - ε) t` (lines 445-446) and then works entirely with the halves. A curve that is C² on `[c, t]` and on `[t, d]` with different one-sided tangents — the corner case `HasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt` was introduced to cover — satisfies the predicate but not this hypothesis, so the only smooth-data intro route offered is unusable exactly where the file's boundedness result is new.

summary: The generic gluing inductions now subsume all their consumers, so the earlier duplication and endpoint-crossing points are resolved or withdrawn. One remaining issue: the C²-to-C^{1,1} introduction lemma assumes a two-sided C² neighborhood that its own proof immediately discards, excluding the corner case the file exists for.
